narrative.hero: How optical measurements shape what machines can infer.
narrative.bio: I study how optical measurements shape what machines can infer, and how to make that inference reliable with limited, noisy data. I connect measurement design, reconstruction and direct inference to understand what makes perception robust. My work on image-free sensing shows that an image need not be the most robust intermediate. I am now applying this measurement-to-inference perspective to time-domain diffuse optical tomography for 3D brain imaging. My long-term aim is to help robots interpret the physical world from raw measurements and physical models.
narrative.welcome: I welcome research collaborations in AI for Science and Science for AI, especially at the interface of physical measurement and machine intelligence. I am also interested in physical and embodied AI, and in how reliable perception and physical reasoning could contribute to artificial general intelligence (AGI). Research internship opportunities are welcome.

projects.title: The Lift Spectrum · Robust image-free sensing
projects.summary: Image-free sensing can be more robust to measurement noise than reconstructing an image first.
bullets: Developed a content-adaptive 1D-to-2D lift and task-prioritized loss scheduling for image-free single-pixel segmentation.

Mapped the noise-dependent crossover against clean-trained reconstruction-first baselines: 3.1–21.7 percentage-point gains in foreground mIoU at 3.13% sampling and 20 dB Gaussian measurement noise across three simulated datasets; optical-bench proof of concept.
highlights: +3.1–21.7 pp foreground mIoU at 20 dB Gaussian noise, 3.13% sampling
Reconstruction-first still leads without measurement noise
Proof of concept on a real single-pixel bench, no fine-tuning
projects.context: Single-pixel segmentation · clean training, noisy testing
detail_points: Robustness: direct inference overtakes the strongest tested reconstruction-first baselines as measurement noise increases, when all models are trained on clean data.
Representation: a content-adaptive 1D-to-2D lift turns the measurement sequence into spatial task features.
Training: task-prioritized loss scheduling (TPLS) shifts emphasis from auxiliary reconstruction to the sensing task.

conditions: All headline models were trained on clean data. Each scene has 128 × 128 pixels and 512 natural-order Hadamard measurements (3.13% sampling). The noisy condition uses 20 dB additive Gaussian measurement noise calibrated on the AC-coupled bucket signal.

The values are foreground mean intersection-over-union (mIoU) differences in percentage points, reported over three training seeds. Each condition uses its strongest tested reconstruction-first baseline. The clean values reverse the sign of the paper’s reported baseline lead so that every row follows the same subtraction.

This comparison uses the paper’s fixed acquisition and normalization. Noise-aware retraining can restore reconstruction-first performance near the training calibration; see Table III in the same section.

projects.title: Sparse Hadamard single-pixel imaging
projects.summary: Tunable sparse Hadamard patterns preserve orthogonality and improve noise resilience, supported by a sparsity-dependent noise model.
bullets: Designed tunable sparse Hadamard patterns that preserve orthogonality, two training-free operating modes and a sparsity-dependent noise model; validated in noise simulations and through-scattering optical experiments.
highlights: Orthogonal sparse patterns built from lower-order Hadamard bases
Sparsity-dependent noise theory tested in simulation and optical experiments
projects.context: Measurement design · theory and optical experiments

projects.title: LDGI · Ghost imaging for optical phased-array line patterns
projects.summary: Loop differential ghost imaging corrects spatial noise asymmetry in ghost imaging with one-dimensional optical phased-array line patterns.
bullets: Developed loop differential ghost imaging for one-dimensional optical phased-array line modulation, with a noise-symmetry metric, numerical simulation and optical validation using spatial-light-modulator-generated patterns.
highlights: Algorithm designed for optical phased-array line modulation
A metric that quantifies the spatial symmetry of noise
Validated in simulation and with SLM-generated line patterns
projects.context: Optical validation with spatial-light-modulator-generated line patterns

platform_copy.linkedin_about:
I am a PhD student at Xi'an Jiaotong University. I study how optical measurements shape what machines can infer, and how to make that inference reliable with limited, noisy data. I connect measurement design, reconstruction and direct inference to understand what makes perception robust.

My work examines how measurement structure and task representation affect robustness. In single-pixel sensing, it shows that an image need not be the most robust intermediate: when models are trained on clean data, direct segmentation can withstand measurement noise better than reconstructing an image first.

My background also includes electro-optic device modeling and optical-system integration. I develop open-source tools for research experiments and review for computational imaging and optics journals.

I am now applying this measurement-to-inference perspective to time-domain diffuse optical tomography for 3D brain imaging. My long-term aim is to help robots interpret the physical world from raw measurements and physical models.

I welcome research collaborations in AI for Science and Science for AI, especially at the interface of physical measurement and machine intelligence. I am also interested in physical and embodied AI, and in how reliable perception and physical reasoning could contribute to artificial general intelligence (AGI). Research internship opportunities are welcome.
platform_copy.linkedin_about_zh:
我是西安交通大学博士研究生。我研究光学测量如何塑造机器的推断能力，以及如何从有限、受噪声影响的测量中获得可靠推断。我的工作将测量设计、图像重建与直接推断联系起来，探究感知鲁棒性的来源。

我关注测量结构和任务表征如何影响鲁棒性。在单像素感知中，我的研究表明，图像未必是最稳健的中间表征：当模型以无噪声数据训练时，直接分割可以比先重建图像再分割更好地抵御测量噪声。

我也具备电光器件建模与光学系统集成经验，开发服务科研实验的开源工具，并担任计算成像与光学期刊审稿人。

目前，我正把从测量到推断的研究思路应用于面向脑部三维成像的时域漫射光学层析成像。长期希望让机器人结合原始测量与物理模型理解物理世界。

欢迎围绕 AI for Science（人工智能赋能科学）与 Science for AI（科学启发人工智能）开展研究合作，尤其关注物理测量与机器智能的交叉问题。我也对物理人工智能（Physical AI）与具身智能（Embodied AI）感兴趣，希望探索可靠感知与物理推理对通用人工智能（AGI）研究的潜在贡献。同时期待研究实习机会。
